dedupe_keys.name: fragility function database for oregon lifelines cascadia lifelines program

description: This DesignSafe project holds the research report and fragility function database built for Oregon lifelines, covering electric power, water and wastewater, and transportation systems for the hazards that matter in Oregon: earthquake, tsunami, landslide, liquefaction and winter storm. The database collects functions from public sources such as HAZUS, IN-CORE, SYNER-G and the Portland Bureau of Environmental Services and from published literature, and records for each its development method, probability distribution, damage states, infrastructure description, regional applicability and source; the study also rates their quality and lists missing functions. Oregon State University produced it for the Cascadia Lifelines Program, a cooperative of Oregon lifeline providers, and it is available as a free download from DesignSafe-CI under the Open Data Commons Attribution licence (April 2022), with a linked web-based Fragility Function Viewer. Caveats: coverage is aimed at Oregon and Cascadia hazards, and the functions are compiled from other studies, not newly derived. Simulation uses: selecting damage functions for water pipes, pump stations and treatment plants in hazard exposure, cascading failure and resilience models. Related: the SYNER-G fragility functions, catalogued by the built environment piece.
